Rashi on Zevachim 10b:32:1.hebrew: כל דמים: החיצונים שנכנסו להיכל לכפר — פסולין. ואף על גב דלא כתיב אלא 'וכל חטאת אשר יובא מדמה וגו'', מרבה רבי עקיבא קדשי קדשים וקדשים קלים מריבויא ד'כל' ו'כל' לקמן ב'כל הזבחים שנתערבו' (זבחים דף פב.):
Rashi on Zevachim 10b:32:1.english: All blood: This is referring to the external blood that entered the Sanctuary to atone, which is disqualified. This is so even though the verse only states: “And any sin offering, any of whose blood is brought, etc.” Rabbi Akiva includes Most Holy Offerings and Lesser Holy Offerings by expounding the superfluous words “kol” and “kol” (all) in the verse cited later in the chapter “In all mixed offerings” (Zevachim 82a).

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:10:1.hebrew: דם דמה לא דריש - דכיון דלא מצי למיכתב "וכל חטאת אשר יובא אל אהל מועד" — דאיצטריך למיכתב "דם" למעוטי בשר — אורחיה דקרא למיכתב "מדמה":
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:10:1.english: He does not expound “blood” and “its blood” [as separate terms] - For since [the verse] could not have written “And any sin offering which is brought to the Tent of Meeting,” [because] it needed to write “blood” in order to exclude the flesh, the way of the verse is to write “of its blood.”

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:13:1.hebrew: קדש קדשים היא כחטאת וכאשם - במנחה הוא דכתיב, וקא א"ר שמעון: מדקא מקיש מנחות לחטאת ואשם, להכי מקיש [לשניהם, לומר לך דיש מהם כחטאת ויש מהם כאשם] שתהא מנחת חוטא כחטאת, דלא לשמה פסולה, ומנחת נדבה כאשם, דכשר שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:13:1.english: "It is most sacred, as the sin offering and as the guilt offering" - It is written with regard to a meal offering, and Rabbi Shimon is saying [this] because the verse compares meal offerings to the sin offering and the guilt offering. For this reason it compares [them to both] [to tell you that some of them are like a sin offering and some of them are like a guilt offering], so that a sinner's meal offering is like a sin offering, in that [if offered] not for its own sake it is disqualified, and a voluntary meal offering is like a guilt offering, in that [if offered] not for its own sake it is fit.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:14:1.hebrew: אלא לרבי אליעזר - כיון דחטאת ואשם כי הדדי נינהו, למאי הלכתא איתקש מנחה לתרוייהו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:14:1.english: But according to Rabbi Eliezer - Since a sin offering and a guilt offering are equivalent to one another, for what halakha is [a meal offering] juxtaposed to both of them?

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:15:1.hebrew: שלא בכלי שרת - שלא קדש הקומץ בכלי שרת, פסולה. שהמנחות הוקשו לזבחים ליטעון ארבע עבודות: קמיצה כנגד שחיטה, מתן קומץ בכלי שרת כנגד קבלת הדם, הולכה כנגד הולכה, הקטרה כנגד זריקה:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:15:1.english: Not in a service vessel - That is, the handful was not sanctified in a service vessel, [the offering] is unfit. For the meal offerings were juxtaposed to the animal sacrifices, so as to require four services: the taking of the handful corresponds to the slaughter; placing the handful in a service vessel corresponds to the receiving of the blood; conveying corresponds to conveying; burning [on the altar] corresponds to the sprinkling.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:15:2.hebrew: ור"ש מכשיר - אם הוליכו בידו, בקומצו, עד המזבח, והקטירו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:15:2.english: And Rabbi Shimon deems [it] fit - If he carried it in his hand, in his handful, to the altar and offered it up [there].

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:1.hebrew: כחטאת וכאשם - להכי איתקש מנחה לחטאת ולאשם, שאינן שוין בהלכותיהן, לומר לך:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:1.english: As the sin offering and as the guilt offering - For this reason the meal offering is compared to both the sin offering and the guilt offering, which are not equal in their laws: to tell you [that the meal offering follows each in its respective case].

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:2.hebrew: בא לעובדה - כשבא לעשות את עבודת המנחה בהלכות והקטרות ביד, שלא בכלי:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:2.english: Comes to perform it - [When he comes to perform the rites of the meal offering] in the rites of bringing near and burning, by hand, without a vessel.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:3.hebrew: עובדה בימין - שהקומץ בה כזריקת דם חטאת, שהיא ביד, באצבע, ובימין. דכתיב בחטאת: "ולקח הכהן מדם החטאת באצבעו ונתן" וגו', ודרשינן לקמן בפ"ב (זבחים דף כד.): "באצבעו ונתן" — שלא תהא נתינה אלא בימין, דכל מקום שנאמר אצבע וכהונה אינו אלא ימין:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:3.english: Its performance with the right [hand] - For the scooping of the handful in it is like the sprinkling of the blood of a sin offering, which is done by hand, with the finger, and with the right [hand]. As it is written regarding the sin offering: "And the priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put" etc., and we expound below in the second chapter (Zevachim 24a): "With his finger, and put" — that the putting should be only with the right [hand], for anywhere that "finger" and "priesthood" are stated, it is only the right [hand].

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:4.hebrew: בא לעובדה בכלי - רשאי לעובדה בשמאל: להוליך הכלי שקדשה בתוכו בשמאלו למזבח, וליתן בשמאלו מן הכלי על האשים, כזריקת דם אשם שהוא מן הכלי למזבח, שאינה בנתינת אצבע, דלא כתיב אצבע אלא בחטאת. וכשרה בשמאל לר"ש בכל הזבחים חוץ מחטאת, דאמרינן לקמן בפרק שני (שם:): זרק בשמאל פסול, ור"ש מכשיר חוץ מחטאת, משום דרבי שמעון תרתי בעי — אצבע וכהונה, דגמרינן ממצורע דכתיב ביה אצבע וכהונה וימין: "וטבל הכהן באצבעו הימנית". ובזריקת כל הזבחים לא כתיב בו אצבע אלא כהונה, חוץ מחטאת:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:16:4.english: If he comes to perform it with a vessel - He is permitted to perform it with the left hand: to carry the vessel in which he sanctified it in his left hand to the altar, and to place [the contents] with his left hand from the vessel onto the fires, like the throwing of the blood of a guilt offering, which is from the vessel to the altar, which is not [done] by placing with a finger, for "finger" is written only regarding a sin offering. And it is valid with the left hand, according to Rabbi Shimon, in all sacrifices except a sin offering, as we say later in the second chapter (there): If he threw with the left hand, it is invalid; but Rabbi Shimon declares it valid, except for a sin offering, because Rabbi Shimon requires two things — a finger and priesthood — which we derive from the leper, regarding whom "finger," priesthood, and right [hand] are written: "And the priest shall dip his right finger." But regarding the throwing of all [other] sacrifices, only priesthood is written, not a finger — except for a sin offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:18:1.hebrew: מנחת חוטא כתיב בה כי חטאת היא - גבי שמיעת הקול, בויקרא:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:18:1.english: Regarding the meal offering of a sinner, “for it is a sin offering” is written - In the passage of one who hears a voice (of adjuration), in Leviticus.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:19:1.hebrew: ולרבנן - הם דפליגי עליה דר' אליעזר במתני', אם כן למאי הלכתא איתקש אשם לחטאת כו':
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:19:1.english: And according to the Rabbis - who disagree with Rabbi Eliezer in the mishna, for what halakha [is the guilt offering juxtaposed with the sin offering]? Etc.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:19:2.hebrew: חטאת - כתיב בה (ויקרא ד׳:כ״ד) וסמך ידו על ראש החטאת:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:19:2.english: A sin offering - It is written regarding it (Leviticus 4:24): “And he shall place his hand on the head of the sin offering.”

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:1:1.hebrew: עולה נכנס דמה לפנים כשרה - בין לרבנן בין לרבי אליעזר, דלא דרשינן כל וכל, והיקשא נמי ליכא הכא:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:1:1.english: A burnt offering whose blood entered inside is valid - Both according to the Rabbis and according to Rabbi Eliezer, for we do not expound "any" and "all," and there is also no analogy (heikesh) here.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:20:1.hebrew: אמרו דבר אחד - דרבי אליעזר נמי פסיל באחרים הנשחטים לשם פסח בזמנו, ולשם חטאת כל ימות השנה. ומברייתא דלקמן דייק לה רבי יוחנן:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:20:1.english: They said the same thing - For Rabbi Eliezer too deems unfit other offerings that are slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering at its [proper] time, and for the sake of a sin offering all the days of the year. And Rabbi Yochanan derives this from the baraita below.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:21:1.hebrew: ורבה אמר באחרים לשם חטאת פליגי - יוסף בן חוני ורבי אליעזר. ולא פסיל רבי אליעזר אלא באחרים לשם פסח, אבל באחרים לשם חטאת מכשיר, כדתניא כו'. ובין רבה ובין ר' יוחנן דייקי מילתייהו מהא מתני', ובמסקנא בעינא לפרושי דיוקייהו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:21:1.english: And Rabba said: They disagree about other [offerings slaughtered] for the sake of a sin offering - Yosef ben Ḥoni and Rabbi Eliezer. Rabbi Eliezer only disqualifies [other offerings] slaughtered for the sake of a Paschal offering, but [with regard to] other [offerings slaughtered] for the sake of a sin offering, he deems them fit, as it was taught in a baraita, etc. Both Rabba and Rabbi Yoḥanan derive their statements from this mishnah, and in the conclusion [of the passage] I will want to explain their inferences:

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:22:1.hebrew: הפסח שעברה שנתו - דתו לא חזי לפסח, והוא סתמיה שלמים, כדרבינן לעיל (זבחים דף ח:) מקראי:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:22:1.english: A Paschal offering whose year has passed - For it is no longer fit for a Paschal offering, [and] it is, unspecified, a peace offering, as we derived above (Zevachim 8b) from verses.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:22:2.hebrew: ושחטו בזמנו לשמו - דהוה ליה שוחט שלמים לשם פסח:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:22:2.english: And one slaughtered it at its time for its own sake - For it is [a case of] one who slaughters a peace offering for the sake of a Paschal offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:22:3.hebrew: וכן השוחט - אחד מכל הזבחים לשם פסח בזמנו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:22:3.english: And likewise, one who slaughters - any one of all the [other] offerings for the sake of a Paschal offering at its [designated] time.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:23:1.hebrew: אם בשאר ימות השנה שאינו כשר לשמו - כדילפינן לה במסכת פסחים (דף סא.): שחטו קודם חצות פסול, שנאמר "בין הערבים", וכמה פעמים שנה הכתוב לעכב קביעות זמנו בי"ד בין הערבים:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:23:1.english: If, during the rest of the days of the year, when it is not fit for its own sake - As we derive it in tractate Pesachim (61a): If one slaughtered it before midday, it is invalid, as it is stated "between the evenings," and the verse repeated several times to make the fixing of its time — on the fourteenth, between the evenings — indispensable.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:23:2.hebrew: אחרים כשרים לשמו - דרבי אליעזר מודה בו, דלא פליג אלא בזמנו, כדתנן בהדיא. אבל כל ימות השנה, אין שם שחיטת פסח חל על קרבן אחר:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:23:2.english: Other [offerings] are fit for its sake - For Rabbi Eliezer agrees about this, as he disputes only [regarding the Paschal offering's] proper time, as we learned explicitly [in the Mishnah]. But during all the days of the year, the name of a Paschal slaughtering does not take effect upon another offering.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:24:1.hebrew: אמר לו רבי אליעזר או חילוף - אם ק"ו אתה בא לדרוש, יכול אני להחליפו בענין אחר ולומר דבר שאינו, ולהכשיר פסח בזמנו שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:24:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: Or the reverse - If you come to expound by way of a kal vachomer (a fortiori argument), I can reverse it in another manner and state something that is not [the law], and deem the Paschal offering fit at its [proper] time when [slaughtered] not for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:24:2.hebrew: ויוכשר פסח בי"ד שלא לשמו - ובדין הזה אתה יכול להכשיר פסח בזמנו שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:24:2.english: And the Paschal offering should be deemed fit on the fourteenth [of Nisan] not for its own sake - And by this line of reasoning, you could deem the Paschal offering fit at its [proper] time even [if offered] not for its own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:25:1.hebrew: וכן אתה אומר - בתמיה: התדרוש ק"ו ויתכשרו?
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:25:1.english: And so you say - [This is] in astonishment: Would you expound a kal vachomer [a fortiori argument] such that [the other offerings] would be deemed fit?

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:25:3.hebrew: מה לי הוכשרו אחרים כו' יוכשרו אחרים כו' - בתמיה. ומהכא דייק רבי יוחנן למילתיה, ואמר דכי היכי דפסיל רבי אליעזר באחרים לשם פסח, פסיל באחרים לשם חטאת; דהא טעמו דרבי אליעזר משום דהוא פסול לשם אחרים, וה"נ בחטאת איתא. ורבה דייק מסיפא שחזר רבי אליעזר מדין זה ודנו בדין אחר, ומודה דאחרים לשם חטאת כשרים:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:25:3.english: What is it to me that other [offerings] are rendered fit... shall other [offerings] be rendered fit... - [This is said] as a rhetorical question. And from here Rabbi Yochanan derives support for his statement, and says that just as Rabbi Eliezer invalidates other [offerings slaughtered] for the sake of a Paschal offering, so too he invalidates other [offerings slaughtered] for the sake of a sin-offering; for Rabbi Eliezer's reason is that it [the Paschal offering] is unfit for the sake of other [offerings], and this applies equally in the case of a sin-offering. But Rabbah derives from the latter clause that Rabbi Eliezer retreated from this argument and argued from a different argument, and [so] he concedes that other [offerings slaughtered] for the sake of a sin-offering are fit:

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:26:1.hebrew: א"כ - אם אתה פוסל אחרים לשמו בזמנו, הורעת כח פסח ונתת כח בשלמים. שכל השנה, שהיא זמן שלמים, פסח הנשחט לשמו כשר, והיום, שהוא זמן פסח, כל שלמים הנשחטין לשמו פסולין. נמצאת מחשבת שלו גדול כח בשלמים מפסח. וקרא אשכחן דאחמור בפסח מבשלמים, דכתיב ביה "הוא" והכתוב ובכל הזבחים הכשיר שלא לשמן:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:26:1.english: If so - If you disqualify other [offerings] slaughtered for its sake at its proper time, you have diminished the force of the Paschal offering and given force to peace offerings. For all year round, which is the time of peace offerings, a Paschal offering slaughtered for its [peace offering's] sake is fit, whereas today, which is the time of the Paschal offering, all peace offerings slaughtered for its sake are unfit. It turns out that the [disqualifying] intent regarding it has greater force in peace offerings than in the Paschal offering. Yet we find in Scripture that the Paschal offering is treated more stringently than peace offerings, as it is written regarding it "it" [i.e., the Paschal offering itself is disqualified when offered for another's sake], and [the verse] deemed fit all [other] sacrifices [when offered] not for their own sake.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:3:1.hebrew: מנחת חוטא - דקרבן עולה ויורד הוא דשמיעת הקול:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:3:1.english: The meal offering of a sinner - For it is a sliding-scale offering (oleh v'yored) [brought] for [transgressing the oath of] hearing a voice.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:3:2.hebrew: תוכיח - שמכפרת, ואם נכנסה לפנים — כשירה, דלא פסל הכתוב אלא דם:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:3:2.english: Can prove - For it atones, and if it entered inside [the Sanctuary] it is valid, since the verse disqualified only blood.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:4:1.hebrew: ונימא חטאת העוף תוכיח - והכי שפיר טפי, שהוא ממיני דמים, וראויה להוכיח על מיני דמים:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:4:1.english: And let us say: the bird sin offering proves [it] - And this is better still, for it is among the types of blood offerings, and it is fit to prove [a rule] regarding blood offerings.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:4:2.hebrew: חטאת העוף בעיא דר' אבין היא - היכא דהכניס דמה לפנים בצוארה, שאין לדמה קבלה, ומיבעיא ליה בפ' דם חטאת (לקמן זבחים צב:) אם נפסלה בכך או לא, ולא איפשיטא לה:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:4:2.english: The case of a bird sin offering is a dilemma of Rabbi Avin - Where one brought its blood inside while it was still in the neck [of the bird], as its blood has no receiving [vessel]; and [Rabbi Avin] raises the question in the chapter [entitled] "Dam Chatat" (below, Zevachim 92b) whether it is disqualified through this or not, and it was not resolved.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:9:1.english: Its blood - "That which is brought" — [this refers to that which is brought] from its blood.

Rashi on Zevachim 11a:9:2.hebrew: ולא בשרה - שאם נכנס בשרה להיכל, אינה נפסלת:
Rashi on Zevachim 11a:9:2.english: But not its flesh - For if its flesh entered the Sanctuary, it is not disqualified.

Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:13:1.hebrew: מנחת חוטא הרי היא כחטאת - אין זה למד מלמד. דאע"ג דחטאת ילפינן למצוה משלמים לעיל, מכל מקום עכובא בגופיה כתיבי. ומנחת נדבה כאשם — לאו משום דמאשם ילפא למצוה, דמנחה גופה איתקש לשלמים כאשם, אלא למימרא דלא הוי כחטאת:
Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:13:1.english: A meal offering of a sinner is like a sin offering - This is not [a case of] learning from [a source that] teaches. For although we derive the mitzvah [requirement of offering it for its own sake] for a sin offering from peace offerings above, nonetheless the [laws that] invalidate [it] are written regarding [the sin offering] itself. And [as for] a voluntary meal offering [being] like a guilt offering — it is not because it derives the mitzvah from the guilt offering, for the meal offering itself is compared to peace offerings, as [is] the guilt offering. Rather, [the comparison] comes to say that it is not like a sin offering:

Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:16:1.hebrew: בא לעובדה ביד עובדה בימין כחטאת - דכתיב בה אצבע, דילפינן מגזירה שוה ממצורע דאצבע הוי ימין. וא"ת, הלא איבעיא לן פרק איזהו מקומן (לקמן זבחים דף נ.): אי ילפינן היקש מג"ש? ואי מצורע חולין [הוא] הוה אתי שפיר [ולא] קשה למ"ד דבעי למד קדש ומלמד קודש, פרק איזהו מקומן (גם זה שם):
Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:16:1.english: "If he comes to perform it by hand, he performs it with the right hand, like a sin offering" - For it is written regarding it "finger," as we derive through a gezeirah shavah from the leper that "finger" means the right hand. And if you ask: But we raised a question in the chapter Eizehu Mekoman (below, Zevachim 50a): do we derive a heqesh (analogy) from a gezeirah shavah? And if the leper [case] is a non-sacred matter, it would work out well [and] would not be difficult according to the one who says that the one learning must be sacred and the source from which it is learned must be sacred, in the chapter Eizehu Mekoman (that same place):

Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:18:1.hebrew: הכי גרסינן עיקר קרא לכדר' יהודה בריה דרבי חייא הוא כו' - תימה: דבריש מנחות (דף ב:) משמע דאידך דרשא עיקר, דפריך אביי: מכדי מחשבה דפסיל רחמנא, היקישא הוא:
Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:18:1.english: So we read: "The verse comes mainly to [teach] that which Rav Yehuda, son of Rabbi Chiya, [said]..." - This is astonishing: for at the beginning of Menachot (2b) it implies that the other derivation is the main one, as Abaye asks: Since [it is] the matter of intention that the Merciful One disqualifies, it is [derived] from an analogy (hekesha)!

Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:1:1.hebrew: אשם שאינו כליל לא כל שכן - לא שייך למימר "חטאת תוכיח", דאיכא למימר: מה לחטאת — שכן דמה למעלה, ושכן צד כרת, ושכן באה בצבור:
Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:1:1.english: A guilt offering, which is not entirely consumed — all the more so - It is not applicable to say "a sin offering will prove it," for one can respond: What is [the strength] of a sin offering? [It is stronger] since its blood [is applied] above [the red line], and since it involves [the penalty of] karet, and since it comes for the community:

Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:26:1.hebrew: הורעתה כח פסח ונתת כח בשלמים - דבזמן שלמים, פסח לשם שלמים כשר, ואילו בזמן הפסח, שלמים לשם פסח פסולים; והלא יש פסוק בפסח לפסול שלא לשמו, ואילו בשלמים אין פסוק:
Tosafot on Zevachim 11a:26:1.english: You have diminished the force of the Paschal offering and given force to the peace offering - For at the time of [the year when one offers] peace offerings, a Paschal offering [sacrificed] for the sake of a peace offering is valid, whereas at the time of the Paschal offering, peace offerings [sacrificed] for the sake of a Paschal offering are invalid. But surely there is a verse regarding the Paschal offering to disqualify [an offering sacrificed] not for its own sake, whereas regarding peace offerings there is no verse:

Zevachim 11a:12.english: The Gemara resumes its discussion of the dispute in the mishna between Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis. Granted, according to the Rabbis, who say that a guilt offering that one slaughtered not for its sake is fit, that is why a meal offering is juxtaposed with a sin offering, and a meal offering is also juxtaposed with a guilt offering.

Zevachim 11a:17.english: The Gemara asks: And as for Rabbi Shimon, does he expound this verse for this purpose and expound it for that purpose, deriving two different *halakhot* from a single verse?

Zevachim 11a:20.english: The mishna teaches: Yosef ben Ḥoni says: Other offerings that are slaughtered for the sake of a Pesach offering or a ḥatat offering are unfit. Rabbi Yoḥanan says: Yosef ben Ḥoni and Rabbi Eliezer said the same thing, i.e., Rabbi Eliezer agrees with Yosef ben Ḥoni.
